points.headline: Nvidia is now financing the customers that buy its chips.
points.body: It disclosed a $21 billion stake in SpaceX and is putting $1.5 billion into the SoftBank developer building OpenAI's data center, guaranteeing its hardware powers both. Groq raised $350 million to abandon chipmaking for a neocloud business running on Nvidia GPUs.

points.headline: Agents fail in ways the leaderboards hide.
points.body: DeepSeek's top-ranked V4 Flash completed only 53.8% of complex agent tasks across eight harnesses, and a separate eval harness found models are most confident exactly when they are wrong. Gartner expects agentic AI costs to rise fivefold by 2028, since cheaper tokens cannot offset how many a real workflow consumes.

points.headline: An AI wrote a bug at Snowflake and another AI exploited it.
points.body: A GitHub Copilot Autofix commit introduced a CI/CD flaw that an autonomous agent later triggered simply by filing a carefully worded Jira issue. It ran through a bug bounty, but the reporting treats it as the first clean machine-to-machine attack chain.

points.headline: Anthropic answers the AI backlash with watermarks and a trust argument.
points.body: Claude's invisible text watermarking turns out to be a version of DeepMind's open-source SynthID-Text, applied to satisfy Europe's transparency rules. Dario Amodei separately called the public's negative view of AI "fundamentally a crisis of trust" in institutions, not a reaction to safety warnings from AI leaders.

points.headline: Amazon is destructively scanning rare books to train models.
points.body: 404 Media tracked a shipment of rare books to an Amazon AI training facility, confirming the suspicion behind anonymous, price-insensitive bulk orders placed with dealers. Print is valuable precisely because it was never online for earlier training runs.

points.headline: Capital is moving into AI that does physical work.
points.body: Gravis Robotics raised a $200 million Series A from SoftBank to put autonomy software and hardware on excavators and other construction equipment. Uber added Zipline drones to Eats, took a stake in the company, and set a target of one million daily drone deliveries by 2029.
